In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of protein synthesis in vivo in the rat liver.
the regulation of protein synthesis and the mechanisms by which this regulation is accomplished.
the regulation of protein synthesis in mammalian tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the recovery of protein synthesis after inhibition by cycloheximidine is a complex phenomenon which is not simply due to a re-accumulation of ribosomes, but rather involves a series of events including changes in ribosome composition, changes in ribosome function and changes in the rate of synthesis of specific proteins, including albumin and plasma fibrinogens, which are not inhibited by cyclohexamide.
the recovery from cycloheximidine inhibition of protein synthesis in liver is characterized by a differential regulation of synthesis of various proteins.

the stimulation of nascent-polypeptides is a consequence of the inhibition of albumin synthesis, and that the recovery of the latter is the cause of the subsequent inhibition of nascent-polypetide synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is an initial period of inhibition of amino acid incorporation into both intra-and extra-cellular proteins, followed by a recovery of incorporation of amino acid into intra- and extra- cellular proteins.
the inhibition of protein synthesis in vivo is followed by a recovery period in which protein synthesis in liver is stimulated to levels above normal for a period of up to 48-72 h.

the recovery of protein synthesis in rat liver following cycloheximidine treatment is not due to the reactivation of a single enzyme or to the recovery of a single protein, but is the result of the coordinated regulation of a number of enzymes involved in the initiation and elongation phases of protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of cyclohexamide in vivo are complex and depend on the type of protein being synthesized and the time after administration of the inhibitor.
protein synthesis in liver is regulated in vivo by a complex series of events that are not easily predicted from in vitro studies.

cycloheximidine treatment results in a complex and time-dependent pattern of protein synthesis in liver, with a period of inhibition followed by a period of stimulation, the latter lasting for up to 2 days after the administration of the drug.
